sources.names.given: Opened 2026-10-17 as CSV/XLSX: (a) Births, Deaths and Marriages Victoria, 'Popular Baby Names' (top 100 male and top 100 female names registered in Victoria per calendar year, with counts), years 2008 to 2025, 18 XLSX files from https://discover.data.vic.gov.au/dataset/popular-baby-names, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0. Victoria's series starts in 2008, so the cohorts born 1952 to 2007 are NSW's, the neighbouring state's, as a stand-in (names by era are alike across the south-east states; this is a known approximation, not Victoria's own). Cohorts: 1930 (PLACEHOLDER: the years 1952 to 1959, the earliest the source has; the true 1930s-1940s names such as Margaret, Joan, John, Kenneth are not in it), 1946 (NSW 1952 to 1965; 1946 to 1951 not in the source), 1966 (NSW 1966 to 1980), 1981 (NSW 1981 to 1995), 1996 (NSW 1996 to 2007), 2008 (Victoria 2008 to 2016), 2017 (Victoria 2017 to 2025). sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.

No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: Private-landlord renters' housing costs as a share of gross household income, 2019-20: 25% or less 57.7%; over 25 to 30% 11.8%; over 30 to 50% 20.7%; over 50% 10.0% (2,535 thousand households; ABS, Housing Occupancy and Costs, 2019-20, released 25 May 2022, cube 5 'Housing costs as a proportion of income ranges', Table 5.1, https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/housing/housing-occupancy-and-costs/2019-20/5.%20Housing%20costs%20as%20a%20proportion%20of%20income%20ranges.xlsx, opened 2026-10-16). The bands are the cube's, rounded to add to 10,000: the cube's cut points are 25, 30 and 50% (not the 20, 30 and 50% the placeholder used), so the under-a-fifth band is gone. All renters: 59.5, 12.2, 19.2 and 9.1%. National; households with nil or negative income are left out. Replaces the placeholder (56, 23, 15, 6%), which put 21% over three tenths against 30.7% here. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.
sources.support.take_up_bps: pension 64%: DERIVED from an opened page: on 28 March 2025, 62% of people aged 65 and over received income support and 91% of those the Age Pension, so about 56% of those 65 and over (26% at 65-69, 59% at 70-79, 80% at 85 and over; AIHW, Australia's welfare, Income support for older Australians, https://www.aihw.gov.au/reports/australias-welfare/income-support-older-australians, opened 2026-10-12); the pension starts at 67, so the two years before it are taken out of the denominator by a rough twelfth (to confirm against DSS payment demographics by single age). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.ownership.owner_bps_by_age: Home ownership by age of the household reference person, Census 2021, national: 36% at 25-29, 50% at 30-34, 72% at 50-54 (AIHW, Australia's welfare, Home ownership and housing tenure, https://www.aihw.gov.au/reports/australias-welfare/home-ownership-and-housing-tenure, opened 2026-10-12); 79.4% at 65 and over (a search summary of ABS Census 2021 reporting: to confirm). The bands between are not filled: 35 to 49 is read at the 30-34 figure and under 30 at the 25-29 figure, which understates both. To replace from the Census table by ten-year bands. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): only as how much likelier a household of one age is than another to be among the town's owners; their number is the houses the profile's house_owner_bps makes owner-occupied. 2026-10-16 (not applied): ABS, Housing Occupancy and Costs 2019-20, cube 2, Table 2.1 (opened, national, a survey; household reference person), gives ten-year bands: 15-24 10.4%; 25-34 40.7%; 35-44 56.7%; 45-54 72.0%; 55-64 79.1%; 65-74 81.7%; 75 and over 83.0% (65 and over 82.4%, computed from the counts). These agree in shape with the Census 2021 figures above (30 and over 50% sits inside 41 to 57%; 65 and over 82% against 79.4%, 3 points higher); the Census is Victoria's neighbour in time (2021) and the cube is a 2019-20 survey, so the Census figures stay and the bands are here to replace them in a refinement.

sources.tenancy.possession: Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (Vic): a notice to vacate may be given once rent is 14 days or more in arrears, of 14 days (Consumer Affairs Victoria, Late or unpaid rent: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, for the 14 days' arrears, that paying by the date ends the notice, that the rental provider must then apply to VCAT, that payment plans can be ordered, and that only the police carry out an order; the 14-day notice period, s 91ZM and ss 330 to 331 to confirm). possession_days 14, plan_months 6 and warrant_days 14 (a warrant of possession is to be executed within 14 days of issue: to confirm) are PLACEHOLDERS for VCAT's practice. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4300: the renter attended, or someone attended for them, at 43% of 822 hearings observed in 2023 ('Key Findings: VCAT hearing observations dataset', opened by a research agent 2026-10-12; applicants were the housing authority and community housing providers, so social and not private landlords; its publisher was not found: to confirm; older Victorian figures it cites run from 20% to 28% for private renters, secondary). plan_consider 'must': the tribunal must be satisfied that possession is reasonable and proportionate, and may adjourn or dismiss an application for arrears where other arrangements can be made (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 'Evictions and possession orders', opened 2026-10-12; the sections, Residential Tenancies Act 1997 ss 330A and 331, recalled, to confirm). 2026-10-16: nothing new was found for possession_days, warrant_days or eviction_notice_days (Consumer Affairs Victoria's pages were reached but the section's text did not extract; the statute was not opened).

sources.employment.hours: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth): ordinary hours are a maximum of 38 a week (s 62), and a change to an employee's hours needs the employee's agreement or an award, enterprise agreement or contract term that allows it; s 524 lets an employer stand an employee down without pay only for industrial action, equipment breakdown or a stoppage the employer cannot reasonably be held responsible for, and a want of ordinary trade is not clearly one (to confirm: legislation.gov.au would not open; read from search results 2026-10-13). So here: only with the employee's agreement, any hours, no spell limit, pay for the hours worked only. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first. 2026-10-16: the Fair Work Ombudsman's 'Stand downs' page (opened) agrees that the Act lets an employer stand employees down, unpaid, only for a stoppage it cannot be held responsible for (equipment breakdown, industrial action, a government direction), not for lack of trade (s 524 wording: search summary); an award, enterprise agreement or contract may allow stand-down or changes in hours, so 'consent' is the Act's floor and not every employee's position (https://www.fairwork.gov.au/pay-and-wages/stand-downs).
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth) s 117 (notice: 1 week under a year's service, 2 from one year, 3 from three, 4 from five; a further week for those over 45 with two years is left out), s 119 (redundancy pay: 4 weeks from one year, rising to 16 at nine years and 12 from ten), s 121 (none owed by an employer of fewer than 15) (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it. 2026-10-16: opened at the Fair Work Ombudsman and found to agree: redundancy pay by years of service (4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16 weeks for 1 to 9 years, 12 from 10) ('Redundancy pay', https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ending-employment/redundancy/redundancy-pay); the small business threshold of fewer than 15 employees, counting associated entities and regular casuals ('Who doesn't get redundancy pay'); notice of 1 week up to 1 year, 2 weeks to 3 years, 3 to 5 years, 4 after 5, plus a week for those over 45 with 2 years' service ('Notice and final pay', https://www.fairwork.gov.au/ending-employment/notice-and-final-pay): the law's bands start at 'more than' a year where the table starts at 'from', so the edges are off by a band for a day, and the over-45 week is left out. The Fair Work Act text itself was not opened (AustLII refused).

sources.outlook.residence: How long people have lived at their current address (starting attachment to the place; docs/behaviour/citizen.md). sources.job_move: What holds someone in a job they have: another must pay premium_bps more before it is worth moving, and per_year_bps more for each year in the job, up to cap_years; and other_trade_bps more again for a job in another line of work (starting over). sources.nature.species: Placeholders for growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection. Gliders and fairy-wrens live in family groups sharing a home range, which isn't modelled, so their breeding threshold is one; frogs breed where at least four share a pond (a home range of half a hectare). How far each crosses ground it can’t live on (dispersal_m): frogs up to 200 m from water (the frog’s guidelines above); gliders glide gaps of tens of metres (75 m, a placeholder); fairy-wrens, placeholder. The young always leave their parents' home range (natal dispersal, in the physics); the share of adults moving a year is a placeholder. sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. Who reports and who doesn't varies (the service-request literature, e.g. Stowers 2022, State and Local Government Review); a rate is to be sourced.
sources.public_service.wage_per_pay_period: [MIXED] Victorian Local Government Award 2015 (MA000132) Level 4 minimum was about $1,068 a week in 2025 (FWC wage draft; opened via search), about $1,119 after the 4.75% 2026 review; councils' enterprise agreements pay clerical Band 4 officers above the award, roughly $78-85k a year. Taken as $80,000 a year, $3,077 a fortnight (to confirm against a council EA).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.administra: [MIXED] Victoria's 79 councils employ about 37,000 EFT (MAV local government facts, search summary) for 6.9m people, about 5.4 per 1,000; the profile's works/waste crew takes part of that. Administration set at 3.0, about 55% of the total, after leaving out works, libraries and community services (share estimated, to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.courts: [PLACEHOLDER] VCAT (civil and residential tenancies lists) has about 600 staff plus several hundred full- and part-time members for 6.9m residents; annual report 2024-25 not opened for numbers. Estimated 0.12 per 1,000, with the Magistrates' Court civil list partly counted. 2026-10-16 (not applied): VCAT alone is 'about 500 members and staff' (VCAT Annual Report 2024-25, p 2), about 0.07 per 1,000, of the 0.12 here; the Magistrates' Court's civil share is not measured. Council staff, the administration split, the other offices' staff, the public service wage and the payment system price: searched, nothing found.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.oversight: [PLACEHOLDER] Victorian Ombudsman (about 130 staff) plus the consumer-affairs regulator and dispute-resolution staff (a few hundred, shared with other work) over 6.9m residents. Estimated 0.06 per 1,000; headcounts from memory, not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.elections: [PLACEHOLDER] The Victorian Electoral Commission keeps roughly 250 permanent staff outside election periods (from memory, to confirm) for 6.9m residents, about 0.036 per 1,000.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.land_regis: [PLACEHOLDER] Land Use Victoria's titles and registry work is roughly 300 staff statewide (estimate, to confirm); over 6.9m residents it is about 0.045 per 1,000.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.press: [PLACEHOLDER] A regional or suburban local paper serving about 20,000 people with a three-person editorial team (editor and two reporters) gives 0.15 per 1,000; typical of small Australian mastheads, not from a dataset.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.banking: [PLACEHOLDER] Australian banks and credit unions employ about 150,000 people for 27m residents (5.5 per 1,000), most in head offices and call centres. A local retail bank's branch, lending and payments staff set at 2.5 per 1,000; estimate, ABS and APRA figures not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.utilities: [PLACEHOLDER] Victoria's metropolitan and regional water corporations employ about 6,000 for 6.9m people (about 0.9 per 1,000); a retailer's operations add roughly 0.3. Total 1.2, estimated from memory of corporation annual reports (to confirm).
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.union: [PLACEHOLDER] About 1.4m Victorian union members; roughly 1 paid officer or organiser per 1,500-2,000 members across unions gives about 700-900 staff, but local organisers are fewer. Set at 0.15 per 1,000; no source opened.
sources.public_service.licences.payment_system: [PLACEHOLDER] A core-banking and payments platform costs a small bank an estimated A$10-20 per customer a year in vendor fees; taken as $15 (1,500 cents) per resident. No vendor price list found; honest guess.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.property_m: [PLACEHOLDER] Carried over unchanged to every profile: property managers (people who run let homes for their owners) at about one to every 100 to 150 let homes is an industry rule of thumb (to confirm, not opened); a town here has about 380 homes for 1,000 people, so about 3 per 1,000 residents. A manager looks after the letting offices of several landlords.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.audit: [PLACEHOLDER] Estimated from the real audit office headcount over the population it serves: Victorian Auditor-General's Office (VAGO), roughly 200 to 250 staff from memory, over 6.9m residents: about 0.035, rounded to 0.04. Headcount from memory, not opened (to confirm). Basis: Audit Act 1994 (Vic) (annual financial audits of councils and state agencies; performance audits); the Australian National Audit Office (Auditor-General Act 1997 (Cth)) audits the Commonwealth side, including the support office, and is not counted here.
sources.audit.office: [MIXED] Victorian Auditor-General's Office, established under the Audit Act 1994 (Vic); the Commonwealth's Australian National Audit Office under the Auditor-General Act 1997 (Cth). Named from memory, not opened (to confirm). The neutral name is the platform's.
sources.audit.answer_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] The Auditor-General's information-gathering powers in the Audit Act 1994 (Vic) carry no fixed number of days that was opened; 28 days is a typical figure for statutory requests (from memory, to confirm).
sources.audit.report_within_days: [PLACEHOLDER] Councils' financial statements go to the Auditor-General for audit within about three months of the year's end and the audit report follows; 120 days is an estimate from memory (Local Government Act 2020 (Vic) and Audit Act 1994 (Vic); not opened; to confirm).
sources.audit.bodies: [PLACEHOLDER] Periods: decisions every 90 days (a quarter) and accounts every 180 days (an interim, half-yearly examination between the annual audits, so that a year of the run holds two), in line with annual financial audit under INTOSAI ISSAI 1000/2000 and an audit sample of 15% of the period, at least 6 and at most 25 decisions, a size chosen for a town of 1,000 to 100,000 under ISA 530 audit sampling (not opened; to confirm). The support office is the outside world's, so only its decisions are checked; the town finance office is checked on accounts. The chosen sample share is the platform's, not the law's.
sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Real places mostly give these appointments to a state body, a minister or a board, none of which the town models, so the council stands in for them (to confirm per place). The paper, which the town keeps on a grant as it keeps the courts, is counted with them (2026-10-25; WM-7). Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.
sources.unions.membership_bps: ABS, Trade union membership, August 2024: 13.1% of employees; by industry, manufacturing 9.0%, construction 11.7%, retail trade 7.0%, public administration and safety 23.1% (the industry figures to confirm against the release's tables); `other`, the overall rate. Keyed by the industries employers' postings name.
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Act 2009 (Cth), s 174: a member may resign by written notice, which takes effect two weeks after it's received (or at once, if the member is no longer eligible; to confirm against the section). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once (a voluntary association; a club's own rules may ask for notice). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: about $14 a week, around what large Australian unions charge full-time members (to source).
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more. Settlements are measured against the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations' Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining (average annualised wage increases in new agreements), a calibration target.
sources.households.age_bands_bps: ABS, Census 2021 QuickStats, Rest of Vic. (GCCSA 2RVIC): people by five-year age group (median age 43); 85 and over taken to 99. The ages of adults living alone, as couples without children at home, or in groups are drawn from this, less the parents the family shares imply (the generator derives it: docs/behaviour/households.md).
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.groups.kinds: The kinds of social group the ABS General Social Survey counts (sport or physical recreation; religious or spiritual; arts or heritage; craft or practical hobby; other recreational or special interest: the category list to confirm against the survey's glossary). How often each meets, and for how long, are placeholders. Whether people come is theirs: the survey's participation is a calibration target (targets), not a rate given to anyone.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Calibrated (2026-09-30): the share of adults who belong to a group at the start (which kind: evenly, a placeholder) and go to its gatherings; after that, whether anyone goes is theirs. The survey counts anyone who took part over 12 months (ABS, General Social Survey 2019: 50.0% of people aged 18 and over), which is more than belong at any one time, so it is the target (targets), not this share. At 50% here, a year's participation came out at 60%.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content, for belief to attach to (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 5). The congregation's stands for the Christian denominations together (one congregation per town is a simplification).
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: ABS, Census of Population and Housing 2021: 43.9% of people reported a Christian affiliation (to confirm against the release; other religions, 10.0%, aren't represented yet). At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less; after that it strengthens, spreads and fades.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.households.child_max_age: The census counts children of any age living with their parents; the ABS family coding counts full-time students to 24 as dependent children. Children at home are drawn up to 24 (a simplification: older children at home are left out).
sources.automation: (PB-6) The outside world's offers of systems to businesses (docs/behaviour/automation.md). Prices are those of vendors in US dollars, converted at an approximate 2026 rate of 1.55 AUD to the dollar (to confirm; the rate is not the place's own and is not read by any code), into the currency's smallest unit; they are the outside world's, held at today's level unless a yearly change is given, like world prices. self-service-point: a bank of self-checkout or self-ordering units: set-up about US$15,000 (a unit's list price runs US$15,000 to 25,000 installed in retail trade reports; to confirm), a yearly licence and support about 16% of it (support contracts run 10 to 20% of the hardware; to confirm), three years' licence, US$3,000 to leave. It does a share of the task 'serve' (scope: placeholder, 30%, in the range of the share of a retail worker's tasks that Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin and Rock 2023 find exposed to current systems; to confirm) in as long as a person takes (placeholder). production-cell: an automated line or cell: set-up about US$90,000 for a cell (the installed cost of an industrial robot system is a few times the robot's price of about US$50,000: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics; to confirm), a yearly licence and maintenance about 10% of it, five years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it does 35% of the task 'make' (placeholder) in 70% of a person's time (placeholder). oversight_hours_per_month and error_bps are placeholders (what looking after one costs the buyer's own staff; how often it gets a unit wrong, refunded at the unit's price). case-handling-system: a system that writes an office's routine papers (a rates notice, a permit decision) and records them: set-up about US$40,000 and a yearly licence of 30% of it (a public-sector case-management system's price; placeholder, to source), three years' licence, a fifth of the set-up to leave; it writes them in 15% of a clerk's time (placeholder) and can do 60% of them (placeholder, in the range Eloundou et al. 2023 give for clerical work; to confirm). Mistakes: 2% of papers (placeholder; automated administration's error rates are a documented risk: Michigan's Auditor General found most fraud determinations of its unemployment system wrong, 2016 (to confirm)).
sources.automation.price_fall_bps_per_year: 0: the outside world's prices for systems are held at today's level (the default); a scenario (worlds/scenarios/falling-system-prices.yaml) gives a yearly fall, with its basis.
sources.automation.firms: (PB-6) How a business weighs a system (docs/behaviour/automation.md). payback_months: the months over which the costs of changing (set-up, exit) must be repaid, 24 for a small business and 36 for a large one (ten staff or more): placeholders, in the range firms report requiring for equipment of two to three years (Graham and Harvey 2001, 'The theory and practice of corporate finance', Journal of Financial Economics; to confirm). hurdle_bps: the margin by which the saving must beat the cost, 20% (placeholder, a margin of safety for a manager's own estimate being unsure). reference_bps: each business already using it that the vendor names eases the hurdle by 2 points, never below nothing (Mansfield 1961, 'Technical change and the rate of imitation', Econometrica; Griliches 1957; Rogers 2003: uptake follows how many have taken it up; the size is a placeholder). on_cost_bps: what staff cost beyond their wage, 0: the world models no employer's charges beyond the wage and redundancy pay. most: the most systems of one kind it takes at once (placeholder).
sources.automation.procurement: Victoria: a council's procurement policy must tender contracts above a threshold; the Local Government Act 2020 (Vic) s 108 asks for a policy, and councils' policies commonly set A$300,000 for services (to confirm; not opened).
